div.p: Each PersonalRelationship resource records a single, unidirectional relationship between two individuals. If the inverse relationship also needs to be recorded, it is represented by a separate PersonalRelationship resource. Properties such as confidence, period, and asserter are recorded independently and can differ between the two directions.

Some relationship types imply an inverse relationship, but do not determine its most specific type. For example, "father of" implies "child of", but does not establish whether the child is a son or daughter. Likewise, "child of" implies "parent of", but not specifically mother or father. Recording one direction does not automatically create a PersonalRelationship resource for the inverse direction.
The family relationship examples use Patient resources for Jane, John, and Mary, and four separate PersonalRelationship resources:
Note: Not all relationships are included in each diagram. The tables and linked resources show the relationships explicitly recorded in these examples.

Each PersonalRelationship describes only one direction. The daughter and mother relationships between Mary and Jane are recorded explicitly, rather than relying on an inferred inverse. Confidence applies only to the relationship on which it is recorded; omitting it does not assert certainty.

The extended and blended families below are separate extensions of the simple family above, rather than one combined family. They reuse the Patient resources for Jane, John, and Mary. The foster home is a separate household. All additional relationships explicitly record certain confidence. Each table entry links to an individual PersonalRelationship resource, including a separate resource for the inverse direction.

Jane's parents are Alice and Robert. Jane and John also have a son, Peter, who is Mary's brother; Mary is Peter's sister. Alice and Robert are the maternal grandparents of both Mary and Peter. For this scenario, Jane and John have been married since 2017-06-12. Their husband and wife relationships record this date in period.start. Together with Robert's relationship as Jane's father, these records make the connection explicit: Robert is John's father-in-law and John is Robert's son-in-law. The in-law relationships are recorded separately, and their periods are not specified.

In addition to the parent/child relationships in the simple family, the following resources explicitly record the relationships between the grandparents and their daughter Jane, the grandparents and each grandchild, Peter and his parents, the two siblings, Jane and John as spouses, and Robert and John as in-laws. A grandparent relationship is recorded directly rather than relying on an application to derive it by traversing parent/child relationships.

In this extension of the simple family, Tom is John's biological son from an earlier relationship and Jane's stepson. Jane is Tom's stepmother. Tom and Mary share John as their biological father, so they are half-siblings, not step-siblings. Anna was adopted by Jane on 2015-06-12, before Jane's marriage to John on 2017-06-12. John is also recorded as Anna's adoptive father, but his adoption date is not specified. Mary and Tom are Anna's siblings within the adoptive family.

The relationship types distinguish biological, step, and adoptive parent/child relationships. The generic sister and brother codes used for Anna's sibling relationships do not assert biological kinship. Each relationship is recorded separately, rather than assuming that a relationship with a parent automatically creates relationships with the other children. Both directions of the Jane-Anna adoption relationship record 2015-06-12 in period.start. John's adoptive relationship is recorded explicitly, rather than inferred solely from his marriage to Jane, and its period is not specified.

In a separate household, Emma and David are foster parents of Leo. Leo was placed with them from 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31. Each of the four PersonalRelationship resources below records that interval in period, with certain confidence.

The foster household Group explicitly lists Emma, David, and Leo as members, using membership = enumerated and the household group code. Leo's membership period matches the placement dates, and member.inactive = true indicates that he is no longer a member. Each of the four PersonalRelationship resources references this Group through group, placing the relationship within the context of that household. The Group lists the individuals; the PersonalRelationship resources separately describe their directed relationships, confidence, and applicable periods.

The foster relationship does not by itself assert biological parentage or legal guardianship. The placement has ended, but the relationships can still be retained as historical information. These resources describe the familial relationships, not any care activities performed by Emma or David.
